title: Annotatio II §.VIII: Peter d’Ailly of Cambrai (1414) favors it — Luther admits drawing from him
pass_a_gloss: Until at length Peter d’Ailly, Cardinal of Cambrai, who flourished at the time of the Council of Constance, and by whose hand and counsels John Huss and Jerome of Prague, men of God and Christ’s martyrs, miserably perished, at the start of the 15th Century, namely the year 1414, began more openly to favor it — from whom also Dr. Luther himself confesses he drew the same, in On the Babylonian Captivity Tom. 2 of the Jena Latin Works fol. 263.
pass_b_english: Peter d’Ailly, Cardinal of Cambrai, at Constance (1414) began to favor it more openly — the same whose hand and counsel saw Huss and Jerome of Prague perish.
Luther himself confesses he drew that line from Cambrai (Babylonian Captivity, Jena Latin II fol. 263).
source_text: Donec tandem Petrus de Aliaco Cardinalis Cameracensis, qui Concilii Constantiensis tempore floruit, cujusque manu & consiliis Johannes Hussus & Hieronymus Pragensis, Viri Dei Christique martyres, miserè periêre, initio Seculi XV. Anno scil. 1414. apertius illi favere cœpit, à quo etiam D. Lutherus eandem hausisse fatetur ipsemet Lib. de Captiv. Babyl. Tom. 2. Operum Latinorum Jenensium fol. 263.
